dedupe_keys.name: flusm water balance model for permeable pavements

description: FluSM is a Python water-balance model developed for permeable pavements at the University of Freiburg. It links surface and soil water-balance modules using soil-moisture measurements, rainfall, evapotranspiration and plot parameters. CSV control files identify inputs and output locations, and results contain time-series columns for each monitored plot. The GMD application covers two years at 15 permeable pavements; other locations and periods require their own measurements. These calculations support drainage capacity planning and help calibrate urban runoff simulations. The source is publicly available through GitLab with a Zenodo release. The repository states GPL-3.0 and permits free use, while the archived metadata states GPL-2.0-or-later; users should resolve this discrepancy for their chosen version. A limitation is dependence on suitable observations and infiltration assumptions. The code was written for Python 2.7, with Python 3 compatibility asserted in its README but not tested here. No directly related catalogue record was established. No observations or code archives were downloaded.
inputs: Rainfall, reference evapotranspiration and wet/dry cycles
